item.title: Canadian lakes show contrasting phosphorus trends across climatic regions
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 22 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04113-7

Lake phosphorus increased in Arctic Canada but declined across other climatic regions, with northern increases linked to ground warming and soil erosion, according to a study that combined field measurements with deep learning analysis of Landsat imagery from 15,240 lakes between 1984 and 2025.

item.title: Regionalized greenhouse gas emissions and infrastructure requirements for future global iron and steel production
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 21 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04129-z

Global steel production emits about 3.7 billion tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent annually and could be cut by up to 70% by 2040, but would require vast hydrogen, carbon storage, and electricity infrastructure, according to a global life cycle assessment and scenario analysis.
item.dc:title: Regionalized greenhouse gas emissions and infrastructure requirements for future global iron and steel production
item.dc:creator: Tom Terlouw
Carina Harpprecht
Christian Bauer

item.title: Effusive sedimentary volcanism experimentally reproduced under Martian-like conditions
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 21 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04155-x

Depressurization-induced boiling sustains rather than quenches low-pressure sedimentary eruptions, driving eruptive transport and surface emplacement and providing new insights into mud volcanism on Mars and other planetary bodies, according to experimental, numerical, and thermal modeling analyses.
item.dc:title: Effusive sedimentary volcanism experimentally reproduced under Martian-like conditions
item.dc:creator: Ondřej Krýza
Petr Brož
Jacob Adler
Matthew Sylvest
Manish Patel

item.title: Warming since the Last Glacial Maximum amplifies Northern Hemisphere drought expansion driven by the Pacific Decadal Oscillation
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 21 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04186-4

The Pacific Decadal Oscillation regime shifts modulate the spring precipitation patterns across East Asia and western North America by altering subtropical trough positions, and the drying effect associated with its negative phase is amplified by warming since the Last Glacial Maximum, as revealed by reanalysis and model experiments.
item.dc:title: Warming since the Last Glacial Maximum amplifies Northern Hemisphere drought expansion driven by the Pacific Decadal Oscillation
